scope: Independent read-only review of proposed historical retention commit and single archive branch; no remote mutations or runtime execution.
finding: A retained ref to a commit whose 95 distinct parent IDs are the exact original branch heads preserves every original commit and its Git tree/blob ancestry. The archive index tree need not reproduce each historical product tree because those remain attached to their unchanged parent commits.

authority.support: Git commit objects may have any number of parents; each parent points to an existing commit.
Create-a-commit accepts a parents array and a tree SHA; the documentation publishes no maximum parent count.
Git retains objects referenced through branches, tags and other refs; reachability from the archival branch is the preservation mechanism.

connector_support.additional_parent_shas: array of additional ordered parent SHAs; no array cap declared in exposed schema
connector_support.create_branch: supports creating an archive branch from the resulting existing commit SHA
connector_support.limitation: Documentation and schema support the design, but acceptance of a 95-parent request has not been executed or proven. Only actual create plus readback can establish it.

required_checks_before_any_deletion: Archive branch name does not collide with a preexisting ref.
Original manifest contains all 104 unique branch names and their exact SHA mappings; deduplicated head set contains 95 IDs.
Read back the created commit through GET /git/commits/{sha}; require exactly the expected 95 unique parents, not merely a successful HTTP/tool response.
Read back its tree SHA and exact manifest/README blobs, comparing expected bytes and Git identities.
Read back refs/heads/archive/pre-consolidation-20261028 and require it to point to that verified commit.
Retain the archive ref; exclude it, main and every current canonical/owned branch from deletion.
Immediately before deleting each historical branch, read its live SHA and require equality with that branch's captured manifest SHA. A changed head stays intact until reconciled.
Handle stale stacked PR heads/bases explicitly before branch deletion and preserve closed-versus-merged truth.
After deletion, reread surviving refs and the archive parent set and preserve an exact deletion result ledger.
semantic_boundaries: The new multi-parent commit is a historical retention/index object. Its creation is not product integration, runtime acceptance or adoption of any historical proposal.
The archive must never become a base for product development or a PR intended for main; never merge this archive commit into main. Its index-only tree intentionally omits product files.
Do not retarget old product PRs to the archive branch, because ancestry could make their change status misleading.
Use original immutable commit URLs for historical source viewing. Deleting original branch names can break branch-name URLs even though every commit remains recoverable.
Commit reachability preserves Git commit/tree/blob data. It is not a complete backup of hosted Actions artifacts, repository settings, comments or external/LFS storage.
Do not call the branch protected unless an actual protection/ruleset result was observed. Treat its retention as mandatory, and add branch protection when supported.

fallback_if_95_parents_rejected.strategy: Create a chain or balanced DAG of ordinary two-parent archival commits, each with the same index tree. The final single archive branch points to the last retention commit, whose ancestry covers all 95 original heads.
fallback_if_95_parents_rejected.verification: For this alternate shape, verify every intermediate parent edge and prove all 95 original heads reachable before deleting anything.
fallback_if_95_parents_rejected.no_bypass: Record the actual failed 95-parent attempt separately; do not infer a successful archive from an attempted create.

conclusion: The design can safely reduce branch clutter to main plus archive plus the chosen canonical continuation, provided the stated exact readbacks and per-branch current-head checks succeed. It avoids creating 95 tags without sacrificing Git-history reachability.
